ἐκ.g: from out, out from among, from
ἐκ.long: from out, out from among, from, suggesting from the interior outwards.
ἐκ.sd: literal or figurative; direct or remote)
ἐκ.kj: after, among, X are, at, betwixt(-yond), by (the means of), exceedingly, (+ abundantly above), for(- th), from (among, forth, up), + grudgingly, + heartily, X heavenly, X hereby, + very highly, in, …ly, (because, by reason) of, off (from), on, out among (from, of), over, since, X thenceforth, through, X unto, X vehemently, with(-out)
ἐκ.der: a primary preposition denoting origin (the point whence action or motion proceeds), from, out (of place, time, or cause;
ἐκ.as:
ἐκ (ἐξ),
prep. c. gen.,
from out of, from (see Addendum, p. 492).
This entry is included here, but in the print version the entry is found on p. 492.
ἐκ, before a vowel ἐξ,
prep. c. gen.,
of motion outwards, separation from (opp. to εἰς; = Lat. e, ex), from out of, from among, from.
I. Of Place,
1.of motion, out of, forth from, off from: Jo 6:31, Ac 9:3, Ga 1:8, al.; esp. after verbs of motion, Mt 8:2817:9, Mk 1:257:28, Jo 1:3320:1, Ac 12:7, 1727:30, al.; constr. praeg., σώζειν (διας.) ἐκ, Ju 5, Ac 28:4. Metaph., Mt 7:4, 5, I Pe 2:9; ἐκ τ. χειρός (-ῶν), seq. gen. pers., Lk 1:74, Jo 10:28, 29, 39, Ac 12:424:7, Re 19:2; πίνειν (q.v.) ἐκ; of the place from which an action proceeds, Lk 5:3 (cf. 12:36, Jo 13:4, II Co 2:4).
2. Of change from one place or condition to another: Jo 8:42, Ro 6:1313:11, Re 7:14, al.; c. ellips. of verb of motion, II Ti 2:26, II Pe 2:21, Re 2:21, al.
3. Of separation or distinction from a number, before collective or pl. nouns: Mt 13:47, 49, Jo 12:1, Ac 3:15, I Pe 1:3, al.; after εἷς, Mt 10:29, Lk 17:15, al.; οὐδείς, Jo 7:19, al.; πολλοί, Jo 11:19, al.; τις, Lk 11:15, al.; τίς, Mt 6:27, al.; in partitive phrase as subject of sentence, Jo 16:17; Hebraistically, ἐκ μέσου seq. gen., = ἐκ (Heb. מִתֹּוךְ), Mt 13:49, al.
4. Of position or direction (so in cl. = ἔξω): ἐκ δεξιῶν (v.s. δεξιός); ἐξ ἐναντίας, Mk 15:39 (metaph., Tit 2:8); ἐκ ῥιζῶν (i.e., utterly), Mt 11:20.
II. Of Time,
1. of the point of time from which, from, since: ἐκ γενετῆς, Jo 9:1, cf. Mk 10:20, Lk 23:8, Ac 24:10, al.
2. Of succession in time: ἐκ δευτέρου, a second time, Mk 14:72, al., cf. Mt 26:44; ἡμέραν ἐξ ἡμέρας, from day to day, II Pe 2:8.
III. Of Origin,
1. of nativity, lineage, race: κοίτην (ἐν γαστρί) ἔχειν, Ro 9:10, Mt 1:18; γεννᾶν ἐκ, Mt 1:3ff.; γεννᾶσθαι (γίνεσθαι) ἐκ, Jo 3:68:41, Ga 4:4; ἐκ πνεύματος (θεοῦ), Jo 1:133:5ff., al. ἔρχεσθαι, εἶναι, etc., ἐκ τ. πολέως, Jo 1:44; φυλῆς, Lk 2:36, al.; τ. ἐξουσίας Ἡρῴδου, Lk 23:7; ὁ ὢν ἐκ τ. γῆς, Jo 3:31.
2. Of the author, occasion or source: Mt 5:37, Jo 2:16, Ro 2:29, I Co 8:6, Ga 5:8, al.; ἐκ (τ.) θεοῦ, I Co 7:7, II Co 5:1, I Jo 4:7; ἐκ τ. πατρός, Jo 6:65, al.; ἐκ τ. γῆς ἐστιν, λαλεῖ, Jo 3:31; εκ καρδίας, Ro 6:17, cf. Mk 12:30, I Ti 1:5; ἐκ ψυχῆς, Eph 6:6, Col 3:23; ἐκ πίστεως, Ro 14:23; κρίνειν ἐκ, Lk 19:22, Re 20:12.
3. Of the agent, after passive verbs: Mt 15:5, Mk 7:11, II Co 2:2, al.; freq. in Re after αδικεῖσθαι (2:11), etc.
4. Of cause, dependence, source of supply: τ. πόνου (των), Re 16:10, 11; τ. φωνῶν, Re 8:13; ἐκ τούτου, Jo 6:6619:12 (but v. Meyer, in ll.); ἐκ θεοῦ λαλεῖν, II Co 2:17; ἐκ τ. ἀληθείας εἶναι, Jo 18:37, I Jo 3:19; ὁ ἐκ πίστεως, Ro 3:264:16; οἱ (ὄντες) ἐκ περιτομῆς, Ac 11:2, Ro 4:12, Ga 2:12, Col 4:11; πίνειν ἐκ, Mt 26:29, Mk 14:25, Jo 4:13, al.; θερίζειν, Ga 6:8; μετέχειν ἐκ (= partit. gen.), I Co 10:13; c. inf., ἐκ τοῦ ἔχειν, II Co 8:11.
5. Of material: Mt 27:29, Jo 2:1519:2, Ro 9:21, I Co 11:12, Re 18:12, al.; allied to which is its use of price (= cl. gen.): Mt 27:7, cf. ib. 20:2, Ac 1:18.
IV. By attraction = ἐν (cl.): τὰ ἐκ τ. οἰκιας, Mt 24:17; τ. ἐξ αὐτοῦ δύναμιν, Mk 5:30 (v. Field, in l.); ὁ πατὴρ ὁ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ, Lk 11:13.
V. Adverbial phrases: ἐξ ἀνάγκης, II Co 9:7, He 7:12; ἐξ ἰσότητος, II Co 8:13; ἐκ μέρους, I Co 12:2713:9-12; ἐκ μέτρου, Jo 3:34; ἐκ συμφώνου, I Co 7:5.
VI. in composition, ἐκ signifies,
1. procession, removal: ἐκβαίνω, ἐκβάλλω.
2. Opening out, unfolding: ἐκτείνω; metaph., ἐξαγγάλλω.
3. Origin: ἔκγονος.
4. Completeness: ἐξαπορέω (v. M, Pr., 237), ἐκπληρόω, ἐκτελέω.

ἐκεῖ.long: (a) there, yonder, in that place, (b) thither, there.
ἐκεῖ.as:
ἐκεῖ
adv.,
[in LXX chiefly for שָׁם ;]
1. properly, of place, there: Mt 2:135:24, al.; οἱ ἐ., Mt 26:71; οὗ . . . ἐ., Mt 6:2118:2024:28, Mk 6:10, Lk 12:34; pleonastic, ὅπου . . . ἐ. (= שָׁםאֲשֶׁר, De 4:5, al.), Re 12:6, 14 (cf. Bl., § 50, 4).
2. As often in cl. (Hdt., Thuc., al.), with verbs of motion, for ἐκεῖσε, thither: Mt 2:2217:2024:2826:36, Mk 6:33, Lk 12:1817:3721:2, Jo 11:818:2, 3, Ro 15:24

ἐκεῖνος.sd: that one (or (neuter) thing); often intensified by the article prefixed
ἐκεῖνος.kj: he, it, the other (same), selfsame, that (same, very), X their, X them, they, this, those
ἐκεῖνος.as:
ἐκεῖνος, -η, -ο
(< ἐκεῖ), [in LXX chiefly for הַהוּא ,הוּא, and cogn. forms ;]
demonstr. pron.,
that person or thing (ille), implying remoteness as compared with οὗτος (hic);
1. absol., emphatic he, she, it: opp. to οὗτος, Lk 18:14, Ja 4:15; ἡμεῖς, He 12:25; ὑμεῖς, Mt 13:11, Mk 4:11; ἄλλοι, Jo 9:9; ἐγώ, Jo 3:30; to persons named, Mk 16:[10, 13, 20], Jo 2:21; of one (absent) who is not named, contemptuously (Abbott, JG, §§2385, 2732), Jo 7:119:28; with respect, of Christ, I Jo 2:63:3, al.; referring to a preceding noun, Mk 16:[10], Jo 7:45; resumption of a participial subject, Jo 1:339:3710:1, Ro 14:14, al. (on its reference in Jo 19:35, v. Westc, in l.; Moffatt, Intr., 568; Sanday, Fourth Gospel, 77ff.).
2. As adj., joined, like οὗτος, to a noun with the article: Mt 7:25, Mk 3:24, Jo 18:15, al.; esp. of time, past or future: ἐν τ. ἡμέραις ἐ., Mt 3:1, Mk 1:9, Ac 2:18(LXX), al.; ἐν ἐ. τ. ἡμέρᾳ, esp of the Parousia, Mt 7:22, Lk 6:23, II Th 1:10, II Ti 1:12; adverbially, ἐκεινής (sc. ὁδοῦ) = cl. ἐκεινῇ (Bl., §36, 13), that way, Lk 19:4.

ἐκπορεύομαι.long: I depart from; I am voided, cast out; I proceed from, am spoken; I burst forth, flow out, am spread abroad.
ἐκπορεύομαι.sd: to depart, be discharged, proceed, project
ἐκπορεύομαι.kj: come (forth, out of), depart, go (forth, out), issue, proceed (out of)
ἐκπορεύομαι.as:
ἐκ-πορεύω
[in LXX chiefly for יָצָא ;]
to make to go out; pass. and mid., to go forth: Lk 3:7, Ac 25:4; of demons leaving one possessed, Mt 17:21 (WH om.), Ac 19:12; of excrement, Mk 7:19; seq. ἀπό, Mt 20:29, Mk 10:46; ἐκ, Mk 13:1 (of the dead rising, Jo 5:29); ἐκεῖθεν, Mk 6:11; ἔξω, Mk 11:19; είς, Mk 10:17, Jo 5:29; ἐπί, c. acc pers., Re 16:14; πρός, c. acc pers., Mt 3:5, Mk 1:5; εἰσπορ- (q.v.) καὶ ἐ., Ac 9:28; metaph., to come forth, proceed: of feelings, etc., Mk 7:23; seq. ἐκ, Mt 15:11, 18Mk 7:15, 20, 21, Lk 4:22, Eph 4:29; ῥῆμα, seq. διά, Mt 4:4(LXX); of lightning and flame, Re 4:59:17, 1811:5; a river, Re 22:1; a sword, Re 1:1619:15; a rumour, seq. εἰς, Lk 4:37; of the Holy Spirit, seq. παρά, Jo 15:26.†

ἐκκόπτω.long: I cut out (off, away), remove, prevent.
ἐκκόπτω.kj: cut down (off, out), hew down, hinder
ἐκκόπτω.as:
ἐκ-κόπτω,
[in LXX for כָּרַת, etc. ;]
to cut out, cut off, cut down: of a hand, foot, Mt 5:3018:8; a tree, Mt 3:107:19Lk 3:913:7, 9; fig., of a branch, Ro 11:22; seq. ἐκ, Ro 11:24; metaph., τ. ἀφορμήν (cf. Jb 19:10ἐλπίδα), II Co 11:12.†

ἐκπειράζω.g: I put to the test, make trial of, tempt
ἐκπειράζω.long: I put to the test, make trial of, tempt, try.
ἐκπειράζω.as:
† ἐκ-πειράζω
[in LXX: De 6:168:2, 16Ps 78:18 (נָסָה pi.) * ;]
= cl. ἐκπειράομαι,
to put to the proof or test, make trial of, tempt: c. acc, of God, Mt 4:7(LXX), Lk 4:12(ib.), I Co 10:9; of Christ, Lk 10:25 (Cremer, 497).†

ἐκεῖθεν.as:
ἐκεῖθεν
adv.,
[in LXX chiefly for מׅשָׁם ;]
1. of place, thence: Mt 4:21, Mk 6:1, al.
2. Of time, thereafter (v.s. κἀκεῖθεν).

ἐκβάλλω.g: I throw, cast, put out, banish, bring forth, produce
ἐκβάλλω.long: I throw (cast, put) out; I banish; I bring forth, produce.
ἐκβάλλω.kj: bring forth, cast (forth, out), drive (out), expel, leave, pluck (pull, take, thrust) out, put forth (out), send away (forth, out)
ἐκβάλλω.as:
ἐκ-βάλλω
[in LXX chiefly for גָּרַשׁ pi., also for שָׁלַךְ hi., יָצָא hi., יָרַשׁ hi., etc. ;]
1.to drive, cast or send out, to expel: c. acc rei, mid. (σῖτον), seq. εἰς, Ac 27:38; pass., Mt 15:17; c. acc pers., Mt 21:12, Mk 11:15, al.; δαιμόνια, Mt 7:22, Mk 1:34, al.; id. seq. ἐκ, Mk 7:26; παρά, Mk 16:9; ἐν, Mk 3:22; (ἐν) τ. ὀνόματι, Mt 7:22, Mk 9:38; λόγῳ, Mt 8:16; seq. ἔξω, Jo 6:37; id. c. gen., Mk 12:8, al.; of expulsion from home, Ga 4:30; from the Church, III Jo 10.
2. In LXX and NT (like Heb.הזׄצׅיא and Aram. הַנְפֵּק), to command or cause to depart: Mt 9:38, Mk 1:12 (v. Swete, in l.), ib. Mk 1:435:40, Lk 10:2, Ja 2:25; τ. κρίσιν εἰς νῖκος (to cause to proceed to its goal), Mt 12:20(LXX).
3.to reject (cl.): τ. ὄνομα ὑμῶς ὡς πονηρόν (cf. De 25:14), Lk 6:22; to leave out, Re 11:2.
4.to take, draw or pluck out;
(a) with violence: Mt 7:5, Mk 9:47, Lk 6:42;
(b)to bring forth or out of: Mt 12:35, Lk 10:35.

ἐκπλήσσομαι.long: I strike with panic or shock; I amaze, astonish.
ἐκπλήσσομαι.as:
ἐκ-πλήσσω
(Attic -ττω, Ac 13:12), [in LXX: (pass.) Ec 7:16, (שָׁמֵם hithp.), Wi 13:4, II Mac 7:12, IV Mac 8:417:16 * ;]
1. prop., to strike out, drive away.
2.to strike with panic or shock, to amaze, astonish: pass., Mt 13:5419:25, Mk 6:27:3710:26, Lk 2:48; seq. ἐπί, c. dat. rei, Mt 7:2822:33, Mk 1:2211:18, Lk 4:329:43, Ac 13:12.†
SYN.: " πτωεῖν, to terrify, agitate with fear;
τρεμεῖν, to tremble, predominantly physical;
φοβεῖν, to fear, "the general term," Thayer;
cf. also φρίσσω, to shudder, and v.s. δειλία

ἐκτείνω.long: I stretch out (forth), cast forth (as of an anchor), lay hands on.
ἐκτείνω.as:
ἐκ-τείνω
[in LXX for שָׁלַח, נָטָה, etc. ;]
to stretch out or forth: τ. χεῖρα (as often in LXX), Mt 8:312:1314:3126:51, Mk 1:413:5, Lk 5:136:10Jo 21:18, Ac 26:1; seq. ἐπί, c. acc pers., towards, Mt 12:49; against, Lk 22:53; εἰς ἴασιν, Ac 4:30; of anchors, to cast, Ac 27:30.†

ἑκατόνταρχος.long: a centurion of the Roman army.
ἑκατόνταρχος.sd: the captain of one hundred men
ἑκατόνταρχος.as:
ἑκατοντάρχης (-άρχος, Mt 8:5, 827:54, Lk 7:2, Ac 22:2528:16; cf. M, Pr., 48); -ου
(< ἑκατόν, ἄρχω,), [in LXX for מֵאָהשַׂר ;]
a centurion: Mt 8:13, Lk 7:623:47, Ac 10:1, 2221:3222:2623:17, 2324:2327:1, 6, 11, 31, 43 (cf. κεντυρίως).†

ἑκατοντάρχης.long: a centurion of the Roman army.
ἑκατοντάρχης.sd: the captain of one hundred men
ἑκατοντάρχης.as:
ἑκατοντάρχης (-άρχος, Mt 8:5, 827:54, Lk 7:2, Ac 22:2528:16; cf. M, Pr., 48); -ου
(< ἑκατόν, ἄρχω,), [in LXX for מֵאָהשַׂר ;]
a centurion: Mt 8:13, Lk 7:623:47, Ac 10:1, 2221:3222:2623:17, 2324:2327:1, 6, 11, 31, 43 (cf. κεντυρίως).†

ἐκχέω.long: I pour out (liquid or solid); I shed, bestow liberally.
ἐκχέω.sd: to pour forth; figuratively, to bestow
ἐκχέω.kj: gush (pour) out, run greedily (out), shed (abroad, forth), spill
ἐκχέω.as:
ἐκ-χέω also Hellenistic, ἐκχύνω (in Th.: II Ki 14:14 *), and ἐκχύννω (q.v.)
[in LXX chiefly for שָׁפַךְ ;]
to pour out: φιάλην, Re 16:1-4, 8, 10, 12, 17; κέρματα, Jo 2:15; αἷμα, Mt 23:35 (cf. MM, Exp., xii), Lk 11:50, Ac 22:20, Ro 3:15(LXX)Re 16:6. Pass., αἷμα, Mt 26:28, Mk 14:24, Ac 22:20; οἶνος, Mt 9:17, Lk 5:37; σπλάγχνα, Ac 1:18. Metaph., τ. πνεῦμα, Ac 2:17, 18(LXX), 3310:45, Tit 3:6; ἀγάπη, Ro 5:5 (cf. Si 36:8, ὀργήν); pass., of persons (like Lat. effundor), to give oneself up to (RV, ran riotously in): Ju 11.†

ἐκτινάσσω.long: I shake off; mid: I shake off from myself.
ἐκτινάσσω.as:
ἐκ-τινάσσω
[in LXX for נָעַר ni., pi., etc. ;]
to shake off: κονιορτόν, Mt 10:14; χοῦν, Mk 6:11. Mid.: κονιορτόν, Ac 13:51; ἱμάτια, Ac 18:6 (cf. MM, Exp., iii).†

ἑκατόν.as:
ἑκατόν, οἱ, αἱ, τά
indecl.,
a hundred: Mt 13:8, 23Lk 15:4, al.; κατὰ ἑ, Mk 6:40; εἰς, ἐν ἑ., Mk 4:8, 20

ἐκριζόω.long: I root out, pluck up by the roots.
ἐκριζόω.kj: pluck up by the root, root up
ἐκριζόω.as:
† ἐκ-ριζόω, -ῶ
[in LXX: Jg 5:14 (שֶׁרֶשׁ), Je 1:10 (נָתַשׁ), Ze 2:4 (גָּרַשׁ A, עָקַר BS), Da TH 7:8 (עָקַר), Da LXX 4:11, 23, Wi 4:4, Si 3:949:7, I Mac 5:51, II Mac 12:7 * ;]
to root out, pluck up by the roots: c. acc rei, Mt 13:2915:13Lk 17:6, Ju 12.†

ἐκλάμπω.as:
ἐκ-λάμπω
[in LXX for אוֹר hi., etc. ;]
to shine forth: Mt 13:43.†

ἐκλύομαι.g: I am unstrung, become weak, fail
ἐκλύομαι.long: I loose, release, unloose (as a bow-string), relax, enfeeble; pass: I am faint, grow weary.
ἐκλύομαι.as:
ἐκ-λύω
[in LXX for רָפָה, etc. ;]
1.to loose, release.
2.to unloose, as a bow-string, to relax, enfeeble; pass., to be faint, grow weary: Mt 15:32, Mk 8:3; of mental weariness, Ga 6:9, He 12:3, 5(LXX).†

ἐκκλησία.long: an assembly, congregation, church; the Church, the whole body of Christian believers.
ἐκκλησία.sd: a calling out, i.e. (concretely) a popular meeting, especially a religious congregation (Jewish synagogue, or Christian community of members on earth or saints in heaven or both)
ἐκκλησία.der: from a compound of G1537 (ἐκ) and a derivative of G2564 (καλέω);
ἐκκλησία.as:
ἐκκλησία, -ας, ἡ
(< ἐκ-καλέω), [in LXX chiefly for קָהָל, otherwise for one of its cogn. forms ;]
1. prop., an assembly of citizens regularly convened (in Thuc., ii, 22, opp. to σύλλογος, a concourse): Ac 19:32, 39, 41.
2. In LXX of the assembly, congregation, community of Israel (De 4:10 23:2, al.): Ac 7:38, He 2:12(LXX).
3. NT, esp. of an assembly or company of Christians, a (the) church;
(a) of gatherings for worship: I Co 11:1814:19, 34, 35;
(b) of local communities: Ac 8:3, I Co 4:17; with name added, Ac 8:1, Ro 16:1, I Th 1:1, al.; pl., Ac 15:41, I Co 7:17; τ. Χριστοῦ, Ro 16:16; τ. Ἀσίας, I Co 16:19; τ. ἁγίων, I Co 14:33; εἰπὸν τ. ἐκκλησίᾳ, Mt 18:17 (but v. Hort, Ecclesia, 10); of a house-congregation (DB, i, 431a), Ro 16:5, I Co 16:19, Col 4:15, Phm 2;
(c) of the whole body of Christians: Mt 16:18, I Co 12:28, Eph 1:22, Phl 3:6, al.; τ. θεοῦ, Ac 20:28 (Κυρίου, T, R, mg.), I Co 15:9, Ga 1:13, I Ti 3:15; ἐ. προτοτόκων ἀπογεγραμμένων ἐν οὐρανοῖς, He 12:23.
SYN.: συναγωγή, q.v. (v. Tr., Syn., §i; DB, i, 426; Hort, Ecclesia, esp. 4ff., 107ff.; Hamilton, People of God, ii, 37ff.; reff. s.vv. "Church," "Congregation," in DB and DCG; Cremer, 332).

ἕκαστος.long: each (of more than two), every one.
ἕκαστος.kj: any, both, each (one), every (man, one, woman), particularly
ἕκαστος.as:
* ἕκαστος, -η, ὂν, [in LXX chiefly for אִישׁ;]
each, every (Lat. quisque) ;
(a) with a noun: Lk 6:44, Jo 19:23, seq. κατά, He 3:13, Re 22:2; εἷς ἕ., Eph 4:16;
(b) without a noun: Ac 4:35, Ro 2:6, al.;
(c) partit. gen., Ro 14:12, I Co 1:12, al.; in sing, with pl. verb, Lk 2:3, Ac 11:29, al.; in apposition with pl. noun or pron., Lk 2:3, Jo 16:32, Ac 2:83:26, al.; εἷς ἕ. (Lat. unusquisque), Ac 2:621:26, Col 4:6, al; ἕ. τι ἀδελφῷ (= Heb. אִישׁ לְאָחִיו, Ge 26:31), Mt 18:35 (cf. He 8:11); ἕ. μετὰ τοῦ πλησίον (= אִישׁ אֶל־רֵעֵהוּ, Jg 6:29, al.), Eph 4:25.

ἑκατονταπλασίων.der: from G1540 (ἑκατόν) and a presumed derivative of G4111 (πλάσσω);

ἐκδίδωμι.g: I give out, let, let out for my own advantage
ἐκδίδωμι.long: I give out, let; middle: I let out for my own advantage.
ἐκδίδωμι.sd: to give forth, i.e. (specially) to lease
ἐκδίδωμι.as:
ἐκ-δίδωμι
[in LXX for נָתַן, etc. ;]
1.to surrender, give up, give out.
2.to let out for hire (Hdt.); mid. (as freq. in π.; v. MM, Exp., xii); to let out to one's advantage, Mt 21:33, 41, Mk 12:1, Lk 20:9.†

ἐκλεκτός.long: chosen out, elect, choice, select, sometimes as subst: of those chosen out by God for the rendering of special service to Him (of the Hebrew race, particular Hebrews, the Messiah, and the Christians).
ἐκλεκτός.as:
ἐκ-λεκτός, -ή, -όν
(< ἐκλέγω), [in LXX for בָּחַר (so prob. in Is 28:16, Pr 17:3, for MT בָּחַן), בָּרִיא, etc. ;]

2. As in Inscr. (MM, Exp., xii), chosen; esp. as in LXX, of Israel, elect, chosen of God (Is 65:9, Ps 105:43, al.); so in NT;
(a) of Christ: Lk 23:35 (cf. Is 42:1); fig., λίθος, I Pe 2:4, 6(LXX);
(b) of holy angels: I Ti 5:21;
(c) of Christians: Mt 24:22, 24, Mk 13:20, 22, 27, II Ti 2:10, I Pe 1:1; τ. θεοῦ, Lk 18:7, Ro 8:33, Col 3:12, Tit 1:1; τ. Χριστοῦ, Mt 24:31; ἐ. κυρία, II Jo 1; ἀδελφή, ib. 13; γένος, I Pe 2:9(LXX); κλητοὶ καὶ ἐ. κ. πιστοί, Re 17:14; opp. to κλητός (not so in Epp.; v. Lft. on Col 3:12), Mt 20:16 (T, WH, txt., R, omit) Mt 22:14 (Cremer, 405, 775).†

ἐκτός.g: without, outside, except, the outside, apart from
ἐκτός.long: (a) adv: (1) without, outside, beyond, (2) except, (3) subst: the outside, (b) prep: outside, apart from.
ἐκτός.sd: the exterior; figuratively (as a preposition) aside from, besides
ἐκτός.kj: but, except(-ed), other than, out of, outside, unless, without
ἐκτός.as:
ἐκτός,
adv.
[in LXX Jg 8:2620:15, III Ki 10:13, al. (לִבַד מִן ,מִלְּבַד, Jg 5:28 (בְּﬠַד),Ca 4:1-3 (מִבַּﬠַד לִִ), al, ;]
1. as adv., outside, beyond: τὸ ἐ., c. poss. gen., the outside, Mt 23:26; in late Gk. (v. Deiss., BS, 118), pleonastic, ἐκτός εἰ μή, I Co 14:515:2, I Ti 5:19.
2. With force of prep., c. gen.;
(a)outside of: I Co 6:18, II Co 12:2;
(b)beyond, besides, except: Ac 26:22, I Co 15:27.†

ἐκφύω.g: I put forth, cause to sprout
ἐκφύω.long: I put forth, cause to sprout.
ἐκφύω.as:
** ἐκ-φύω
[in OT (Sm.) Ps 104:14; (Al.) Is 61:11 * ;]
to cause to grow out, put forth (leaves): Mt 24:32, Mk 13:28.†

ἐκδύω.g: I put off, take off, strip off
ἐκδύω.long: I put off, take off, strip off, with acc. of person or garment or both.
ἐκδύω.sd: to cause to sink out of, i.e. (specially as of clothing) to divest
ἐκδύω.der: from G1537 (ἐκ) and the base of G1416 (δύνω);
ἐκδύω.as:
ἐκ-δύω
[in LXX chiefly for פָּשַׁט ;]
to take of, strip of, strip: c. acc pers. (sc. clothing), Mt 27:28; c. acc pers. et rei, Mt 27:31, Mk 15:20, Lk 10:30; mid., to put off: fig., of the body, II Co 5:4.†

ἔκστασις.long: (properly: distraction or disturbance of mind caused by shock), bewilderment, amazement; a trance.
ἔκστασις.sd: a displacement of the mind, i.e. bewilderment, "ecstasy"
ἔκστασις.as:
ἔκ-στασις, -εως, ἡ
(ἐξίστημι) [in LXX: Ge 27:33, I Ki 14:15, Ez 26:16, al. (חֲרָדָה); II Ch 14:1417:1020:29 (פַּחַד), al. ;]
1.a displacement (Arist.).
2. An abnormal condition of the mind, in which the subject passes out of his usual self-control (Hippocr.); in NT (Kennedy, Sources, 121 f.);
(a)a trance: Ac 10:1011:522:17;
(b)amazement: Mk 5:4216:8, Lk 5:26, Ac 3:10.†

ἐκφέρω.long: I bring out, carry out, sometimes out of the city for burial; I bring forth, bear, produce.
ἐκφέρω.as:
ἐκ-φέρω
[in LXX chiefly for יָצָא hi. ;]
1.to carry out, bring out: cc. acc rei, Lk 15:22, I Ti 6:7; c. acc pers., Mk 8:23, Ac 5:15; of the dead for burial (cf. κομίζω), Ac 5:6, 9, 10.
2.to bring forth;
(a) of women (Hipp., Arist., al.);
(b) of the ground (Hdt.): He 6:8.†

ἔκφοβος.as:
ἔκφοβος, -ον
[in LXX: ἔ. εἶναι for יָגֹר, De 9:19; also I Mac 13:2 * ;]
affrighted, terrified: Mk 9:16, He 12:21.†

ἐκθαμβέομαι.long: I am greatly astonished, am awe-struck.
ἐκθαμβέομαι.as:
**† ἐκ-θαμβέω, -ῶ
(< ἔκθαμβος), [in LXX: Si 30:9 * ;]
1.to be amazed.
2.to amaze, terrify (Si 30:9). Pass., to be amazed, terrified: Mk 9:1514:3316:5, 6.†

ἐκθαυμάζω.as:
**† ἐκ-θαυμάζω,
[in LXX: Si 27:2343:18, IV Mac 17:17 * ;]
strengthened form of θαυμ-; to wonder greatly: Mk 12:17.†

ἐκλέγομαι.long: I pick out for myself, choose, elect, select.
ἐκλέγομαι.der: middle voice from G1537 (ἐκ) and G3004 (λέγω) (in its primary sense);
ἐκλέγομαι.as:
ἐκ-λέγω
[in LXX chiefly for בָּחַר ;]
to pick out, choose. In NT always mid. (exc. Lk 9:35, ἐκλελεγμένος, WH, ἀγαπητός, R, mg.), to pick out for oneself, choose (cf. M, Pr., 157 f.): c. acc rei, Lk 10:4214:7; c. acc pers., Ac 6:515:22, 25; of Christ (v. supr.), Lk 9:35; of Christ's choice of disciples, Lk 6:13, Jo 6:7013:1815:16, 19Ac 1:2; of the Divine choice: of persons, Mk 13:20, Ac 1:2413:1715:7, Eph 1:4, Ja 2:5; of things, I Co 1:27, 28 (Cremer, 402, 773).†

ἐκπνέω.long: (lit: I breathe out), I breathe my last, expire.
ἐκπνέω.as:
* ἐκ-πνέω, -ῶ,
to breathe out; sc. βίον, ψυχήν (expressed in cl., Æsch., al.; cf. LS, s.v.), to breathe one's last, expire: Mk 15:37, 39Lk 23:46. For force of aorist, v. Swete, Mk 15:37.†

ἐκκομίζω.long: I carry out (of the city gate for burial).
ἐκκομίζω.as:
* ἐκ-κομίζω
to carry out: as freq., a corpse for burial, Lk 7:12.†

ἐκμάσσω.sd: to knead out, i.e. (by analogy) to wipe dry
ἐκμάσσω.der: from G1537 (ἐκ) and the base of G3145 (μασσάομαι);
ἐκμάσσω.as:
** ἐκ-μάσσω
[in LXX: Si 12:11, Ep. Je13,24 *;]
to wipe off: c. acc, Lk 7:38, 44, Jo 11:212:313:5.†

ἐκζητέω.long: I seek out, seek out after, require.
ἐκζητέω.sd: to search out, i.e. (figuratively)investigate, crave, demand, (by Hebraism) worship
ἐκζητέω.as:
† ἐκ-ζητέω, -ῶ
[in LXX chiefly for דָּרַשׁ, also for נָצַר, בָּקַשׁ, etc. ;]
1.to seek out or after, search for: c. acc pers. (I Mac 9:26); fig., τ. κύριον, θεόν (cf. Ps 14:2, Am 5:4, al.), Ac 15:17, Ro 3:11, He 11:6; εὐλογίαν, He 12:17; ἐξεζήτησαν κ. ἐξηραύνησαν (as in I Mac l.c.), sought and searched out: I Pe 1:10.
2. As in II Ki 4:11, Ez 3:18, 20 al. (דָּרַשׁ), to demand, require: Lk 11:50, 51 †

ἐκτελέω.long: I complete, bring to completion, carry out, perform.
ἐκτελέω.as:
ἐκ-τελέω, -ῶ
[in LXX: De 32:45 (כָּלָה), II Ch 4:5, Da TH 3:40, II Mac 15:9 * ;]
to bring to an end, finish, complete: Lk 14:29, 30.†

ἐκλείπω.long: I fail, die out, come to an end, am defunct.
ἐκλείπω.as:
ἐκ-λείπω
[in LXX for כָּלָה, כָּרַת ni., תָּמַם, etc., 47 different words in all ;]
1. trans., to leave out, pass over.
2. Intrans., to leave off, cease, fail: μαμωνᾶς, Lk 16:9; πίστις, Lk 22:32; ἔτη, He 1:12(LXX); of the sun in an eclipse, Lk 23:45.†

ἐκμυκτηρίζω.g: I deride, scoff at, mock greatly
ἐκμυκτηρίζω.long: I deride, scoff at, mock greatly.
ἐκμυκτηρίζω.as:
† ἐκ-μυκτηρίζω
[in LXX: Ps 2:422:735:16 (לָעַג), I Es 1:51 A* ;]
to hold up the nose in derision at, scoff at: c. acc, Lk 16:1423:35.†

ἐκδικέω.g: I give justice over, defend, avenge, vindicate
ἐκδικέω.long: I give justice over, defend, avenge, vindicate.
ἐκδικέω.as:
† ἐκδικέω, -ῶ
(< ἔκδικος), [in LXX for פָּקַד, נָקַם, שָׁפַט, etc. ;]
1.to vindicate: c. acc pers., Lk 18:3, 5.
2.to avenge: c. acc pers., ἑαυτούς, Ro 12:19; c. acc rei, παρακοήν, II Co 10:6; αἷμα, Re 6:1019:2 (Cremer, 203; for exx. from π. in both senses, v. MM, Exp., xii).†

ἐκδίκησις.long: (a) a defense, avenging, vindication, vengeance, (b) full (complete) punishment.
ἐκδίκησις.as:
† ἐκ-δίκησις, -εως, ἡ
(< ἐκδικέω), [in LXX chiefly for נָקָם ;]
vengeance, vindication: Lk 21:22, Ro 12:19 (v. MM, Exp., xii), He 10:30(LXX), II Co 7:11; of the injured person, c. gen., Lk 18:7, 8; c. dat., Ac 7:24; of the offender, c. gen. obj., I Pe 2:14; c. dat., II Th 1:8 (cf. Si 12:6).†

ἐκκρέμαμαι.long: I hang out, mid: I hang upon.
ἐκκρέμαμαι.sd: to hang upon the lips of a speaker, i.e. listen closely
ἐκκρέμαμαι.der: middle voice from G1537 (ἐκ) and G2910 (κρεμάννυμι);

ἐκχωρέω.long: I go out, depart from, withdraw, flee.
ἐκχωρέω.as:
εκ-χωρέω, -ῶ
[in LXX: Nu 16:45 (רוּם ni.), Jg 7:3 (צָפַר), Am 7:12 (בָּרַח), I Es 4:44, 57, I Mac 9:62 * ;]
to depart, withdraw: Lk 21:21.†

ἐκφεύγω.g: I flee out, away, I escape
ἐκφεύγω.long: I flee out, away, escape; with an acc: I escape something.
ἐκφεύγω.as:
ἐκ-φεύγω
[in LXX for נוּס, etc. ;]
to flee away, escape: absol., Ac 16:27, I Th 5:3, He 2:3; seq. ἐκ, Ac 19:16; c. acc pers., He 12:25; c. rei, Lk 21:36, Ro 2:3; τ. χεῖρας αὐτοῦ, II Co 11:33.†

ἐκτενέστερον.der: neuter of the comparative of G1618 (ἐκτενής);

ἐκνεύω.long: I escape, get clear of, deviate, withdraw.
ἐκνεύω.sd: (by analogy) to slip off, i.e. quietly withdraw
ἐκνεύω.as:
ἐκ-νεύω
[in LXX: Jg 4:18 (סוּר) Jg 18:26, IV Ki 2:2423:16 (פָּנָה), Mi 6:14 (סוּג hi.), III Mac 3:22 * ;]
1.to bend the head aside (Xen.).
2.
(a)to shun, avoid (Diod.);
(b)to withdraw: Jo 5:13†

ἐκκεντέω.der: from G1537 (ἐκ) and the base of G2759 (κέντρον);
ἐκκεντέω.as:
ἐκ-κεντέω, -ῶ
[in LXX chiefly for דָּקַר ;]
1.to prick out, put out (Arist.).
2.to pierce (Polyb., LXX): c. acc pers., Jo 19:37(LXX), Re 1:7.†

ἔκδοτος.sd: given out or over, i.e. surrendered
ἔκδοτος.der: from G1537 (ἐκ) and a derivative of G1325 (δίδωμι);
ἔκδοτος.as:
** ἔκ-δοτος, -ον
(< ἐκδίδωμι), [in LXX: Da TH Bel 1:22 * ;]
given up, delivered over: Ac 2:23 (for construction, v. Field, Notes, 111 f.).†

ἔκθαμβος.as:
**† ἔκ-θαμβος, -ον
(< θάμβος), [in LXX: Wi 10:19, Da TH Da 7:7 (dreadful, terrible: אֵמְתָּנִי) * ;]
amazed (cf. Polyb., xx, 10, 9): Ac 3:11.†

ἐκψύχω.g: I breathe my last, die, expire
ἐκψύχω.long: I breathe my last, die, expire.
ἐκψύχω.as:
ἐκ-ψύχω
[in LXX: Jg 4:21 A (עוּף), Ez 21:7 (כָּהָה pi.)* ;]
to expire, breathe one's last: Ac 5:5, 1012:23 (cf. ἐκπνέω; Cremer, 906).†

ἔκθετος.long: cast out, exposed (to the elements), abandoned.
ἔκθετος.sd: put out, i.e. exposed to perish
ἔκθετος.der: from G1537 (ἐκ) and a derivative of G5087 (τίθημι);
ἔκθετος.as:
** ἔκ-θετος, -ον
(< ἐκτίθημι), [in Al.: Ez 42:3 * ;]
cast out: ποιεῖν ἔ. = ἐκτιθέναι, Ac 7:19.†

ἐκτίθημι.g: I put out or expose a child, set forth, explain
ἐκτίθημι.long: (a) I put out or expose a child, (b) mid: I set forth, expound, explain.
ἐκτίθημι.as:
ἐκ-τίθημι
[in LXX for נָתַן ni., etc. ;]
to set out, expose: Ac 7:21, Metaph., to set forth, expound: Ac 11:428:23; c. acc rei, Ac 18:26.†

ἐκλογή.g: a choosing out, selecting, choice by God
ἐκλογή.long: a choosing out, selecting, choice (by God).
ἐκλογή.as:
** ἐκλογή, ῆς ἡ
(< ἐκλέγω), [in Aq.: Is 22:7; Sm., Th.: Is 37:24 * ;]
a choice, selection; in NT, always of the Divine choice (EV, election): σκεῦος ἐκλογῆς, gen. qual., a chosen vessel; κατ ἐ., Ro 9:1111:5, 28; c. gen. pers., I Th 1:4, II Pe 1:10; by meton., ἡ ἐ. = οἱ ἐκλεκτοί, Ro 11:7.†

ἐκτενῶς.as:
ἐκτενῶς
adv.,
[in LXX: Jh.3.8 (חׇזְקָה), Jl 1:14, Jth 4:12, III Mac 5:9 * ;]
fervently, earnestly: Ac 12:5, I Pe 1:22; compar., Lk 22:44 (WH br., R, mg., omits).†

ἐκπίπτω.g: I fall out, fall off, fall away, fade away, wither away
ἐκπίπτω.long: I fall out, fall off, fall away; hence in nautical language: I fall off from the straight course; of flowers: I fade away, wither away; I fall from, lose, forfeit; I am cast ashore; I am fruitless.
ἐκπίπτω.sd: to drop away; specially, be driven out of one's course; figuratively, to lose, become inefficient
ἐκπίπτω.kj: be cast, fail, fall (away, off), take none effect
ἐκπίπτω.as:
ἐκ-πίπτω
[in LXX: Is 40:828:1, 4 (הֶבֶל), Jb 14:2 (מָלַל, v. RV. mg), Jb 15:30 (סוּר), Jb 15:33 (שָׁלַךְ hi.), etc. ;]
to fall out of, fall from, fall off: seq. ἐκ τ. χειρῶν, Ac 12:7; absol., Ac 27:32; of the withering of flowers (as LXX, ll c.), Ja 1:11, I Pe 1:24(LXX); of navigators falling off from a straight course, Ac 27:17, 26, 29. Metaph., c. gen. rei: Ga 5:4, II Pe 3:17; absol., fall from its place, fail, perish: Ro 9:6.†

ἐκπέμπω.as:
ἐκ-πέμπω
[in LXX for שָׁלַח ;]
to send forth: Ac 13:417:10.†

ἐκπληρόω.g: I fill completely, fulfill in every particular
ἐκπληρόω.long: I fill completely, fulfill in every particular (to the utmost), make good.
ἐκπληρόω.as:
** ἐκ-πληρόω
[in LXX: II Mac 8:10, III Mac 1:2, 22 * ;]
1.to fill full, make up a number.
2.to fulfil (MM, Exp., xii; Cremer, 839), Ac 13:32.†

ἐκδιηγέομαι.der: from G1537 (ἐκ) and a compound of G1223 (διά) and G2233 (ἡγέομαι);
ἐκδιηγέομαι.as:
ἐκ-δι-ηγέομαι, -οῦμαι depon.,
[in LXX chiefly for סָפַר, pi. ;]
to tell in detail, relate, declare: Ac 13:41(LXX)15:3.†

ἐκπηδάω.as:
ἐκ-πηδάω, -ῶ
[in LXX: De 33:22 (זָנַק), etc. ;]
to spring forth: εἰς τ. ὄχλον (cf. Ju 14:17), Ac 14:14 (for ex. in π., v. MM, Exp., xii).†

ἐκπλέω.long: I sail out (of harbor), sail away.
ἐκπλέω.as:
* ἐκ-πλέω, -ῶ
to sail away: Ac 20:6; seq. εἰς, Ac 15:3918:18.†

ἐκταράσσω.as:
ἐκ-ταράσσω
[in LXX: Ps 18:4 (בּﬠת pi.), Ps 88:16 (צמת), Wi 17:3, 418:17 * ;]
to throw into great trouble, agitate: Ac 16:20.†

ἐκδέχομαι.sd: to accept from some source, i.e. (by implication) to await
ἐκδέχομαι.as:
ἐκ-δέχομαι
[in LXX for עֶרֶב, קָבַץ, etc. ;]
1.to take or receive from (Hom., Hdt., a1.).
2. (Rare in cl.), to expect, await: c. acc rei, Jo 5:3, He 11:10, Ja 5:7; c. acc pers., Ac 17:16, I Co 11:3316:11; seq. ἕως, He 10:13 (Cremer, 687).†

ἐκεῖσε.as:
ἐκεῖσε
adv.,
[in LXX: Jb 39:29מׅשָׁם * ;]
thither: Ac 21:3; constr. pregn. (MM, Exp., xii; Field, Notes, 134), τοὺς ἐ. ὄντας, Ac 22:5.†

ἐκπλήρωσις.as:
**† ἐκ-πλήρωσις, -εως, ἡ)
[in LXX: II Mac 6:14 * ;]
a completion, fulfilment: Ac 21:26.†

ἐκλαλέω.as:
** ἐκ-λαλέω, -ῶ
[in LXX: Jth 11:9 * ;]
to speak out, divulge: Ac 23:22.†

ἐκτένεια.as:
**† ἐκ-τένεια, -ας, ἡ
(< ἐκτενής), [in LXX: Jth 4:9, II Mac 14:38, III Mac 6:41 * ;]
zeal, intentness, earnestness (cf. Deiss., BS, 262): Ac 26:7.†

ἐκβολή.long: a throwing out, a jettisoning of cargo to lighten a ship.
ἐκβολή.sd: ejection, i.e. (specially) a throwing overboard of the cargo
ἐκβολή.as:
ἐκ-βολή, -ῆς
(< ἐκβάλλω), [in LXX: Ex 11:1 (גָּרַשׁ), Jos 1:5 (ἐκβολὴν ποιεῖσθαι, טול hi.), Ez 47:8 (יָצָא)* ;]
1.a throwing out.
2.a jettison, a throwing overboard of cargo: Ac 27:18 (cf. Jos, l.c.; and v. Field, Notes, 144 f.).†

ἐκκαίομαι.as:
ἐκ-καίω
[in LXX chiefly for בָּעַר ;]
1.to burn up.
2.to kindle. Pass., to burn: metaph., of the passions (cf. Si 16:6, Jb 3:17), Ro 1:27.†

ἐκκλίνω.g: I fall away from, turn away
ἐκκλίνω.long: (lit: I bend away from), I fall away from, turn away (from), deviate.
ἐκκλίνω.sd: to deviate, i.e. (absolutely) to shun (literally or figuratively), or (relatively) to decline (from piety)
ἐκκλίνω.kj: avoid, eschew, go out of the way
ἐκκλίνω.as:
ἐκ-κλίνω
[in LXX for נָטָה, סוּר, etc. ;]
intrans., to turn aside, turn away: metaph., from the right path, absol., Ro 3:12(LXX); from evil, absol., I Pe 3:11; seq. ἀπό, c. gen. pers., Ro 16:17.†

ἐκκλείω.as:
ἐκ-κλείω
[in LXX: ἐ. κρίσιν, for נָטָה hi., Ex 23:2 (also as v.l., Jb 34:20, Ps 67:30 (Ps 68:30) * ;]
to shut out: Ga 4:17. Pass., Ro 3:27.†

ἑκατονταετής.as:
ἑκατονταετής (Rec. έτης), -ές
(< ἑκατόν, ἔτης) [in LXX for שָׁנֶהמֵאָהבֵּן, Ge 17:17 * ;]
a hundred years old: Ro 4:19.†

ἑκών.as:
ἑκών, -οῦσα, -όν
[in LXX: Ex 21:13, Jb 36:19 * ;]
willing, of one's own free will: Ro 8:20, I Co 9:17 (Cremer, 246).†

ἐκπετάννυμι.sd: to fly out, i.e. (by analogy) to extend
ἐκπετάννυμι.der: from G1537 (ἐκ) and a form of G4072 (πέτομαι);
ἐκπετάννυμι.as:
ἐκ-πετάννυμι
[in LXX chiefly for פָּרַשׂ, as Is 65:2 (hithp.) ;]
to spread out (as a sail), stretch forth: Ro 10:21(LXX).†

ἐκκλάω.as:
ἐκ-κλάω, -ῶ
[in LXX: Le 1:17 (שָׁסַע pi.)* ;]
to break off: pass., Ro 11:17, 19, 20.†

ἔκδικος.long: avenging, subst: an avenger (the word occurs frequently in the sense of a special advocate [champion] of a city).
ἔκδικος.sd: carrying justice out, i.e. a punisher
ἔκδικος.as:
** ἔκδικος, -ον
(< δίκη), [in LXX: Wi 12:12, Si 30:6, IV Mac 15:29 * ;]
1.without law, unjust.
2.exacting penalty from; as subst., an avenger: Ro 13:4; seq. περί, I Th 4:6 (in π., a legal representative; Milligan, Th., l.c.).†

ἐκκαθαίρω.as:
ἐκ-καθαίρω
[in LXX for בָּעַר, etc. ;]
1.to cleanse thoroughly, cleanse out: c. acc, ἑαυτόν, II Ti 2:21; of the impurity removed, ζυμήν, I Co 5:7.†

ἔκβασις.long: (a) a way out, escape, (b) result, issue.
ἔκβασις.der: from a compound of G1537 (ἐκ) and the base of G939 (βάσις) (meaning to go out);
ἔκβασις.as:
** ἔκ-βασις, -εως, ἡ
(< ἐκβαίνω), [in LXX: Wi 2:178:811:14 * ;]
1.a way out (Hom., Xen.): I Co 10:13.
2.the issue (Menand.) He 13:7.†

ἔκτρωμα.long: (strictly: a lifeless abortion) an untimely birth.
ἔκτρωμα.sd: a miscarriage (abortion), i.e. (by analogy) untimely birth
ἔκτρωμα.der: from a comparative of G1537 (ἐκ) and (to wound);
ἔκτρωμα.as:
ἔκ-τρωμα, -τος, τό
(< ἐκτιτρώσκω, to miscarry), [in LXX: Jb 3:16, Ec 6:3 (נָפַל; also in Aq., Ps 58:9, Nu 12:12 (מוּת) * ;]
an abortion, an untimely birth (v. Field, Notes, 179): I Co 15:8.†

ἐκνήφω.g: I return to soberness of mind
ἐκνήφω.long: I return to soberness of mind.
ἐκνήφω.as:
† ἐκ-νήφω
[in LXX: Ge 9:24, Hb 2:7 (יָקַץ), Jl 1:5, Hb 2:19 (קַיץ hi.), I Ki 25:37 (יָצָא), Si 34 (31)2* ;]
to become sober after drunkenness: metaph., of sobriety of mind, I Co 15:34.†

ἐκδημέω.sd: to emigrate, i.e. (figuratively) vacate or quit
ἐκδημέω.der: from a compound of G1537 (ἐκ) and G1218 (δῆμος);
ἐκδημέω.as:
* ἐκ-δημέω, -ῶ
(< ἔκδημος, from home; cf. -ία, III Mac 4:11)*;
to be from home, absent: II Co 5:6; seq. ἀπό, II Co 5:8; seq. ἐκ, II Co 5:9 (cf. ἀπο-, ἐνδημέω).†

ἐκφοβέω.as:
ἐκ-φοβέω, -ῶ
[in LXX chiefly for חָרֵד hi. ;]
to frighten away, terrify: c. acc pers., II Co 10:9.†

ἐκδαπανάομαι.as:
*† ἐκ-δαπανάω, -ῶ
strengthened form of δαπανάω, to spend wholly; pass., with reflexive force, to spend oneself wholly: seq. ὑπέρ, II Co 12:15.†

ἐκπτύω.g: I spit upon, disdain, reject, loathe
ἐκπτύω.long: I spit out, disdain, reject, loathe.
ἐκπτύω.as:
* ἐκ-πτύω
1.to spit out.
2.to spit at in disgust, to abominate, loathe (= cl. ἀποπτ-, καταπτ-): Ga 4:14.†

ἐκτρέφω.sd: to rear up to maturity, i.e. (genitive case) to cherish or train
ἐκτρέφω.as:
ἐκ-τρέφω
[in LXX for גָּדַל, etc. ;]
1. prop., of children, to nurture, bring up: Eph 6:4.
2.to nourish: Eph 5:29.†

ἐκδιώκω.long: I persecute, expel by persecuting, drive out, vex, harass.
ἐκδιώκω.sd: to pursue out, i.e. expel or persecute implacably
ἐκδιώκω.as:
ἐκ-διώκω
[in LXX for בָּרַח hi., צָמַת, הָדַף, etc. ;]
to chase away, drive out: I Th 2:15 (cf. De 6:19, Jl 2:20).†

ἐκζήτησις.as:
*† ἐκ-ζήτησις, -εως, ἡ
(< ἐκζητέω),
a questioning (RV), subject for dispute: I Ti 1:4.†

ἐκτρέπομαι.long: (lit: I turn out from); mid. and pass: I turn aside (from the right road), wander, forsake, and with an object: I remove from myself, shun, avoid.
ἐκτρέπομαι.sd: to deflect, i.e. turn away (literally or figuratively)
ἐκτρέπομαι.kj: avoid, turn (aside, out of the way)
ἐκτρέπομαι.der: from G1537 (ἐκ) and the base of G5157 (τροπή);
ἐκτρέπομαι.as:
ἐκ-τρέπω
[in LXX for הָפַךְ, Am 5:8 * ;]
to turn out of the course, turn aside, c. acc Pass., with middle sense, intrans., to turn aside: He 12:13 (R, txt., for be put out of joint, R, mg., v. Thayer, s.v. Westc., in l); fig., seq. εἰς, I Ti 1:6; ἐπί, II Ti 4:4; ὀπίσω, I Ti 5:15; c. acc, to shun, avoid: I Ti 6:20.†

ἔκγονον.der: neuter of a derivative of a compound of G1537 (ἐκ) and G1096 (γίνομαι);
ἔκγονον.as:
ἔκ-γονος, -ον
(< ἐκγίγνομαι, to be born of), [in LXX for פְּרִי (neut.), בֵּן, etc. ;]
1. c. gen., born of.
2. As subst., ὁ, ἡ ἔ., a child, son or daughter; in pl., descendants: τέκνα ἢ ἔ., children or grand-children, I Ti 5:4.†

ἔκδηλος.as:
** ἔκ-δηλος, -ον
(< δῆλος), [in LXX: III Mac 3:196:5 * ;]
strengthened form of δῆλος, q.v., quite clear, evident: II Ti 3:9.†

ἐκστρέφομαι.g: I change for the worse, corrupt, pervert
ἐκστρέφομαι.long: I change for the worse, corrupt, pervert.
ἐκστρέφομαι.as:
ἐκ-στρέφω
[in LXX: De 32:20, Am 6:13Ez 16:34 A (הָפַךְ), Za 11:16 (פָּרַק pi.), Ez 13:20 (צוּד pil.)* ;]
1.to turn out of (Hom.).
2.to turn inside out; metaph., to change entirely, pervert (Aristoph.): Tit 3:11.†

ἑκούσιος.long: willing, with right good will, voluntary, spontaneous.
ἑκούσιος.der: neuter of a derivative from G1635 (ἑκών);
ἑκούσιος.as:
ἐκούσιος, -ον
(< έκών), [in LXX chiefly for נְדָבָה, as Nu 15:3 (κατ’ ἑ.);]
usually of actions, voluntary: κατὰ ἑ., of free will (Lft., in l), Phm 14.†

ἑκουσίως.long: willingly, of one's own accord, spontaneously.
ἑκουσίως.der: adverb from the same as G1595 (ἑκούσιον);
ἑκουσίως.as:
ἑκουσίως
adv.,
[in LXX: Ps 54:6 (נְדָבָה) II Mac 14:3, al. ;]
voluntarily, willingly: He 10:26, I Pe 5:2.†

ἐκδοχή.as:
* ἐκ-δοχή -ῆς, ἡ
(< ἐκδέχομαι);
1. in cl.,
(a)a receiving from, succession;
(b)an interpretation.
2. In NT, = προσδοκία, expectation: He 10:27 (cf. Field, Notes, 231; Cremer, 688).†

ἐκβαίνω.as:
ἐκ-βαίνω,
[in LXX for עלח ;]
to go out: He 11:15.†

ἐκλανθάνω.long: I forget entirely, make to forget.
ἐκλανθάνω.der: middle voice from G1537 (ἐκ) and G2990 (λανθάνω);
ἐκλανθάνω.as:
** ἐκ-λανθάνω
[in Sm.: Ps 13:2 * ;]
to escape notice utterly; mid., to forget utterly: He 12:5.†

ἐκτενής.long: intent, constant, strenuous, intense; met: earnest, zealous.
ἐκτενής.as:
** ἐκτενής, -ές
(< ἐκτείνω), [in LXX: III Mac 3:105:29 * ;]
stretched, strained. Metaph., earnest, zealous: I Pe 4:8 .†

ἑκάστοτε.der: as if from G1538 (ἕκαστος) and G5119 (τότε);

ἔκπαλαι.sd: long ago, for a long while
ἔκπαλαι.kj: of a long time, of old
ἔκπαλαι.as:
*† ἔκ-παλαι
adv.
(of a class of compound adverbs common in late Gk.; v. Mayor on 2 Pe, l.c.),
for a long time, from of old: II Pe 2:33:5.†

ἐκπορνεύω.as:
† ἐκ-πορνεύω
[in LXX chiefly for זָנָה, freq. of spiritual unfaithfulness ;]
strengthened form of πoρνεύω, implying excessive indulgence; mid, to give oneself up to fornication: Ju 7.†
